subject: Request: SLO carveout + commercial offset for Stratus deployment
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@stratus.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Production SLO ask for Q1 rollout

Hi Ben (and Sean),

Quick context: we’re ramping Stratus’s customer-facing inference tier in Q1 and the initial multiregional pattern is exposing higher cross-region failover risk than we modeled. Our legal and platform teams need a concrete commercial offset if Redwood can’t meet the 99.9% uptime SLO for the first 12 months.

Specifically we’re asking if Redwood would consider:
- a temporary SLO at 99.5% for 12 months,
- a cap on service credit exposure, and
- a one-time commercial discount in lieu of tighter SLO guarantees.

Can you confirm what Redwood would need for exec approval (if anything) and preferred commercial parameters? We need to include anything you request in the procurement package to our finance team by EOD next Tuesday.

Attachments: none from our side yet — I can share our deployment risk memo if helpful.

Thanks,
Elena Morales
Head of Platform, Stratus AI
elena@stratus.ai

---
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena@stratus.ai>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Production SLO ask for Q1 rollout

Elena —

Appreciate the heads-up and the clear asks. Short answer: we can accommodate a temporary SLO deviation but it requires deal desk and exec signoff because it’s outside our standard commercial guardrails. To move fast, here’s a straw proposal from our side:

- Temporary SLO: 99.5% uptime for the first 12 months after go-live (standard is 99.9%).
- Service credits: standard service credit schedule applies, but we suggest capping aggregate exposure at 5% of monthly recurring revenue (MRR) for the carveout period.
- Commercial offset: one-time implementation credit equal to 7.5% of year-one ACV (we can convert to an invoice credit).
- Operational requirement: customer to accept and sign our accelerated remediation playbook and to commit to Redwood Dedicated reserved capacity for the production pool.

I’ve attached a short SLO proposal (SLO_Proposal_Stratus_v3.pdf) that lays out the technical mitigations and rollback triggers. If you can confirm acceptance of the operational requirements, we’ll route this to deal desk for formal review and to the execs for approval on the commercial concession.

Next steps I propose:
1) Elena — confirm remediation playbook + reserved capacity commitment in writing.
2) Marissa — deal desk to review and prepare an approval note for execs (including trade-offs).
3) Sean — I can loop you into the exec note if we need a faster signoff path.

Happy to jump on a quick call to align.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
Attachments: SLO_Proposal_Stratus_v3.pdf

---
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Deal desk review: Stratus — nonstandard SLO + commercial concession (REQ)

Team —

I reviewed Ben’s straw proposal and the attached SLO doc. Summary for exec consideration:

- Customer: Stratus AI (Priority enterprise prospect, expected ARR $1.2M year 1).
- Ask: temporary SLO change to 99.5% for 12 months + a one-time commercial credit to offset operational risk.
- Proposed concession: 7.5% one-time implementation credit (we can convert to invoice credit), aggregate service credit cap at 5% MRR during carveout.
- Mandatory mitigations: customer signs our accelerated remediation playbook and agrees to reserved capacity (to limit cross-region failover exposure).

Why this is material: the reduction from 99.9% → 99.5% increases potential exposure during high-traffic events. However, the revenue profile and strategic fit (market reference) make this an acceptable targeted concession if we limit financial exposure.

Requested decision: exec endorsement to approve the above parameters. If approved, deal desk will prepare the contract redline and a short unilateral amendment to the SLO schedule.

Attachments: deal_summary_STRATUS.xlsx, SLA_Playbook_STRATUS.docx

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Deal Desk Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

---
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 15:47:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Deal desk review: Stratus — nonstandard SLO + commercial concession (REQ)

Marissa/Sean —

Thanks for the concise note and the financials. I’m comfortable approving a limited carveout with the following binding conditions:

1) Temporary SLO: 99.5% uptime for the first 12 months post-RTM (as proposed).
2) Financial exposure: cap aggregate service credit liability at 5% of MRR for the carveout period.
3) Commercial concession: approve a 7.5% one-time implementation credit (not to exceed vendor margin thresholds).
4) Operational controls: Stratus must sign the SLA_Playbook_STRATUS.docx and provide written confirmation of reserved capacity (Redwood Dedicated) before the carveout is effective.
5) Reporting: bi-weekly incident and remediation updates for the first 90 days post-launch, reviewed by SE and CS.

If Marissa confirms these conditions are included in the contract amendment and Ben secures written confirmation from Elena on the operational controls, this is approved.

Jonas Weber
VP, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai

---
